**What this is.** A look back at the simulation work on chr10 between 2026-09-20 and 2026-09-22. It covers three pieces of work. The first is a
simulation of non-informative founder sites: how alleles written into H_d that a line does not carry change the painting. The second is a
simulated BC1 panel used as a ground-truth picture. The third is the QC-set benchmark (design B), which measures per-donor pooled variant
discovery and genotyping (RTIGER poolseq, PHG lowcopy) against known truth, plus a 6-plant BC2S3 bulk arm. Every number below comes from
the listed sources. If a planned step has no results in them, the text says so.

::: {.callout-note}
## Outcome
- **Non-informative fraction (f).** RTIGER keeps the right calls up to f = 0.15 and then collapses to HET: ALT accuracy is 0.03 at
  f = 0.40 and 0.001 at f = 0.70. Even with a perfect founder, PHG shows a false-teosinte floor of about 1%. The floor is deterministic:
  80 allele-dense ranges carry 86% of it. PHG also puts B73 gaps inside true ALT (5.4% of range calls), and 60% of those gap ranges hold
  zero founder alleles.
- **Design B replaced design A** (2026-09-21). Design A was dropped because it is uninformative for discovery. Design B uses
  tract-structured BC1 pools, the TeoNAM v5 map, breakpoints fixed per line, and an independent read draw at each λ.
- **Lines are 10 families × 1 sib, not 2 × 5.** In the 2 × 5 run all 10 lines descended from two BC2 chromosomes, and chr10 came out all REF.
- **Design B ran end to end for Gigi and TIL18** (chr10). Tables and paintings are in `agent/qcset_designB_results/`. Discovery recall
  for founder A was 0.36 (Gigi) and 0.30 (TIL18), with precision 0.68 / 0.73. RTIGER calls ≈98–99.8% of ranges. PHG calls 15–60%, and
  its false-teosinte length grows with λ.
- **Bulk arm** (6-plant pool, dosage k/12, Gigi) was run and painted. It tests whether the HET/B73 segments interspersed inside real
  introgressions come from bulk sampling of a family that is still segregating. No summary table is recorded, only paintings.
- **Not run / no results recorded:** swap_test (negative control), and the real-read founders (RIL003, RIMH001) with TIL11. TIL11,
  RIL003 and RIMHU001 still need an anchorwave chr10 alignment.
:::

## 1. Non-informative-fraction simulation (2026-09-20)

**Design.** The truth comes from `nilHMM::simulate_family("BC2S3")`: 8 families × 6 sibs on chr10, 20k markers (ALT 4.6%, HET 1.2%, 110
segments). The true H_d is the union strict founder of Zd.0040_P1 (166,789 alleles) minus a random fraction f. The PHG DB was not rebuilt:
one founder serves every f, and only the simulated genomes change. Because the removed sites are non-informative by construction, their
effect is isolated. Reads were simulated with wgsim, 2x150, 0.4x. PHG ran on the union B73+Zd graph with two settings:

- setting A: stay 0.99 / F 0.86 / min-reads 1 (the user's setting)
- setting B: stay 0.9999 / F 0 / min-reads 1 (a contrast)

The nilhmm callers were rtiger and pedigree. binhmm gave no result because its adapter failed on the bin output, so its lane was removed.
That was an adapter issue, not a caller failure. The plan started with f ∈ {0, 0.15, 0.40}, and f = 0.70 was added later that evening
(jobs 896939/40/41).

| caller | ALT acc. f=0 | f=0.15 | f=0.40 | f=0.70 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rtiger | 1.00 | 0.999 | 0.03 (→ HET) | 0.001 (block → HET) |
| pedigree | 0.97 | 0.79 | 0.52 | 0.14 |
| PHG A (0.99/0.86/1) | 0.83 | 0.74 | 0.18 | 0.015 (67% → B73) |
| PHG B (0.9999/0/1) | 0.77 | 0.29 | 0.00 | 0 (→ HET) |

- HET accuracy: rtiger 0.99; PHG B 0.86; PHG A 0.72 → 0.45; pedigree 0.47 → 0.20. B73 accuracy was 0.97–1.00 for every caller.
- For pedigree, non-informative markers became B73 runs: 0.3% / 14% / 34% of true ALT was called B73.
- Mean PHG dosage against a truth of 0.104: A 0.124 / 0.118 / 0.078; B 0.127 / 0.100 / 0.078.

**PHG false-teosinte floor is deterministic** (f = 0, setting A, pure-B73 reads, exact founder). 1.0% of truth-B73 range calls came out
teosinte (2,777 / 275,467). 242 ranges were affected at least once. 80 ranges, each affected in ≥10 of 48 lines, carry 86% of the false
calls, and 12 small ranges (1–25 kb) misfire in all 48 lines. Each line had 45–71 false calls, which matches the ~50–60 het ranges of the
real B73 check. The recorded mechanism is that founder alleles create k-mers that also occur elsewhere on the chromosome. These 80 ranges
have a median of 51 alleles per 7 kb, 5× the typical density. The runlog lists two possible masks: allele density, or a list of ranges
that misfire on a B73-only run.

**Transitions inserted by the model with a perfect founder.** 5.4% of true-ALT range calls are B73/B73. An earlier figure of 9% was
marker-weighted; 5.4% is the range-weighted value. 122 deterministic ranges carry 83% of these gaps, and 60% of those ranges hold zero
founder alleles: every read ties, and at stay 0.99 the tie is broken toward B73. 17% of all union ranges have zero alleles. Two fixes
are recorded: set stay to the genetic value (0.9991 for union ranges, 0.997 for gene-only ranges), or drop zero-allele ranges. The gap
ranges and the false-teosinte ranges do not overlap. The zealtiger simulation fit λ = 4.72/Morgan as the exit rate. Holland's 2/Morgan
is a different quantity (genome-wide junction density).

*Sources: agent/SIM_plan_noninformative_sites_20260920_200135.md; agent/pilot_1B_chr10_runlog_20260917.md (20:50, 21:00, 21:25, and the
f = 0.70 note under 22:03); agent/handover_20260921_025746.md; docs/PROJECT_STATE.md.*

## 2. BC1 panel simulation

`agent/simulate_bc1.R` simulates a 12-individual BC1 panel with `simulate_nil(design = "BC1S0")` over 10 chromosomes (2,000 markers,
m = 1.5, seed 42). It turns the true states into segments and paints the karyotype. The result is true ancestry only, with no calling, and
serves as the ground-truth reference for the real RTIGER mosaic. Its local outputs are `agent/sim_bc1_panel*.png`. The same
`simulate_nil("BC1S0")` call gives the BC1 plants in design B (§3).

*Sources: agent/simulate_bc1.R header; docs/PROJECT_STATE.md ("BC1 panel sim").*

## 3. QC set: design A dropped, design B adopted (2026-09-21)

Design A sampled an inbred founder at each coverage, both as reference-as-donor and as a 1:1 B73 "F1". It was the first plan of
2026-09-21. It was then dropped: with an inbred founder every allele is informative, so a mismatch is only base error. Design B instead
measures the weak point of the real per-donor route: discovery from 6-plant BC1 pools at ~15x, i.e. which false alleles survive and how
they affect skim genotypes at each coverage. With an inbred founder, "non-informative" here means false alleles from pooled discovery
(mapping artifacts, low-dosage misses). It does not mean donor heterozygosity. Standing variation would need a separate experiment with
a heterozygous founder.

| element | design B choice |
|---|---|
| founders (chr10 run) | Gigi (Zd) and TIL18 (Zx), the only two with chr10 MAFs against B73 |
| genetic map | TeoNAM-native v5 (`markers_v5_gwas118k_cm.tsv`; chr10 7,173 markers / 119 cM) |
| BC2S3 lines | 10 = 10 families × 1 sib; breakpoints simulated once per line, shared by the sweep |
| coverage sweep | λ ∈ {0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4, 0.8, 1.2}; each λ an independent read draw over the same tracts |
| BC1 pools | 30 plants `simulate_nil("BC1S0")` → 5 pools of 6, per-tract dosage k/12, 15x, donor reads homozygous |
| witness | merge of the 60 sweep samples (drops alleles no line carries) |
| truth alleles | assembly SNPs vs B73 ∩ lowcopy BED (8,095 ranges, 26.0 Mb) = PERFECT founder |
| founder variants scored | A, A+B (discovered), PERFECT (truth) |
| callers | PHG two-founder graph (0.9991 / F 0.86 / min-reads 1); RTIGER poolseq (rigidity 500, variable sites) |

**Why 10 × 1 and not 2 × 5.** The 2 × 5 run (job 908526) gave all-REF chr10. `simulate_family` descends every family from one BC2 plant,
so all 10 lines rested on two chromosomes and there was nothing to score. The user's words were: "the ten families should derive from 10
different bc1s".

**Founder reads rule** (user, 2026-09-21): use real Illumina only if it is 2x150, like the skims; otherwise simulate 2x150 from the
assembly.

| founder | read source | reason |
|---|---|---|
| RIL003 (Zl) | real SRR18441560, ~24x | 2x150 |
| RIMH001 (Zh) | real SRR18441536, ~23x | 2x150 |
| TIL11 (Zv) | simulate | real runs only 2x100 / 2x75 |
| TIL18 (Zx) | simulate | no WGS at all (TIL25's runs are 2x101, moot once simulating) |
| Gigi (Zd) | simulate | only run is 2x76; the PI 462368 2x150 run is a different plant |

*Sources: docs/PLAN_qcset_simulation_benchmark.md §0–§4, §8; agent/PLAN_qcset_designB_20260921_124826.md; docs/DECISIONS.md (2026-09-21
rows); memory qc-set-founder-reads.md; agent/handover_20260921_155429_simulation_benchmark.md.*

## 4. Design B steps and read budget

The step names are the user's, fixed on 2026-09-21: breakpoint_sim → alignment_sim → build_founder_gvcf → read_mixing →
variant_discovery → imputation (imputation_PHG, imputation_RTIGER) → benchmarking → chr_painting. Code is in `PHG/qcset/`.

**breakpoint_sim** (job 908589, 18 s). 6 of the 10 lines carry donor (0.3–76 Mb) and 4 are pure B73. Genome fractions are REF 0.868 /
HET 0.001 / ALT 0.131. In the BC1 pools, the median is 8 tracts per pool; k = 3 covers 47% of the chromosome, k = 4–6 covers 38%, and
there is no k = 0.

**read_mixing demand table.** All 65 samples per founder draw disjoint reads: 5 pools + 60 sweep samples. `read_mixing.py --plan-only`
computes the peak demand at one locus: 30.5x donor and 86x B73 (5 pools × 15x plus the sweep, Σλ 3.75x × 10 lines). The earlier budget
was 22x donor and 80x B73. The sources were therefore sized at donor 2 × 22x and B73 5 × 20x (44x / 100x). The user chose "add the 5th
slice" over reusing reads or using 4 pools. Each read goes to at most one destination via a hash of its qname, and mates stay together.
Reads are kept only in lowcopy ± 1 kb. Merged samples carry one @RG (ID = SM = sample), because CRISP splits a file into one sample per
RG, which breaks -p 12 pooling.

**alignment_sim.** wgsim 2x150 reads from the chr10 FASTAs were aligned to whole B73 (minibwa -x sr, MAPQ20). The B73 slices took 9 min
each (10.16 M pairs) and kept 86%. TIL18_D took 28 min and kept 43%. The recorded consequence: pools and sweep samples get less donor
depth than nominal in divergent regions. This was intended, because real pools lose the same reads.

| step | state |
|---|---|
| 1 breakpoint_sim | done (908589) |
| 2 alignment_sim | done: tables and paintings downstream exist for both founders; per-slice retention recorded for B73 and TIL18_D only |
| 3 build_founder_gvcf | done (PERFECT `.alt.tsv` read by benchmarking; `discovery_summary.tsv` has the truth counts) |
| 4 read_mixing | done (unit-test output not recorded in the sources) |
| 5 variant_discovery | done: CRISP (5 pools + witness, -p 12) → witness veto → step 4 → founders A, A+B |
| 6 imputation_PHG / RTIGER | done for A, AB, PERFECT |
| 7–8 benchmarking / chr_painting | done; copies in `agent/qcset_designB_results/{Gigi,TIL18}/` |

*Sources: agent/handover_20260921_203500_simulation_benchmark.md; docs/DECISIONS.md; PHG/qcset/README.md and script headers; git log
2026-09-21 (d445c99 … f40c542); agent/qcset_designB_results/ file listing.*

## 6. Bulk arm: 6-plant BC2S3 pool (2026-09-22)

**Question.** Real BC2S3 skims are 6-plant bulks, and inside real introgressions the painting shows interspersed HET and B73 segments.
`breakpoint_sim_bulk.R` tests whether that pattern comes from sampling a still-segregating BC2S3 family as a 6-plant field-plot bulk, as
opposed to sampling one fixed inbred genome. For each plot it takes one `simulate_family("BC2S3", sibs = 6)` draw and emits two matched
arms:

- single-genome control: sib 1, states 0/1/2. This arm must paint clean.
- bulk: all 6 sibs pooled, population dosage k/12. This arm predicts the shredding.

The two arms share founder haplotype and breakpoints, so the only difference between them is residual segregation seen as a bulk.
`read_mixing --sweep-source bulk` then drew the bulk sweep at k/12 for Gigi, reusing the CRAMs, pools, witness and founders. Imputation
reused the existing Gigi graphs (A, PERFECT), and RTIGER ran on the same samples. In the truth lane, HET means a still-segregating region
(0 < k < 12).

The handover of 2026-09-21 02:57 had already recorded that "bulking does not create B73 runs (Poisson sampling)". No summary table is
recorded for the bulk arm. The results are the paintings and the RTIGER CSVs in `agent/qcset_designB_results/Gigi_bulk/`.

![qc05: true genotypes of the 6 BC2S3 plants and their equimolar pool, chr10 (local copy).](../../agent/qcset_designB_results/Gigi_bulk/qc05_plants_and_pool.png)

![Gigi 6-plant pool at 1.2x and 0.05x: truth, RTIGER, PHG per introgressed plot (local copy).](../../agent/qcset_designB_results/Gigi_bulk/Gigi_bulk_introg_by_coverage.png)

**F sweep on qc05.** `f_sweep_qc05.sbatch` reran find-paths on the qc05 pool with founder Gigi_A, reusing its read-mappings, at
F = 0.0 … 1.0 and all six coverages. Paintings exist at λ = 0.05, 0.4 and 1.2. The next script, `real_zd0040_F0.sbatch`, calls F = 0
"the pool-reconstruction setting from the qc05 F sweep". It applied that setting to the 39 real Zd.0040_P1 pools, and a stay × F grid on
real data followed. Those runs are real-data work and fall outside this notebook; their local paintings are in `real_F0/` and
`callers_introg/`.

![qc05 pool at 1.2x: PHG founder-A F sweep, F = 0.0 to 1.0 (local copy).](../../agent/qcset_designB_results/f_sweep_qc05/qc05_Fsweep_lam1.2.png)

## 8. Pending and not run

- **swap_test** (negative control: one founder's sweep genotyped against the other founder, where calls driven by reads must collapse):
  written (fde2c23); no results recorded.
- **Real-read founders** RIL003 / RIMH001, and TIL11: not run. TIL11, RIL003 and RIMHU001 need anchorwave chr10 (~2 h × 8 cpu each)
  before their truth exists. The reads are on hazel: `raw/qc_set/RIL003` has 186,229,307 pairs and `raw/qc_set/RIMH001` has 179,230,099
  pairs, both verified.
- **Whole genome** (≈600 CPU-h, ≈200 without anchorwave): not needed for the benchmark's conclusions (plan §5b).
- A one-page summary of design B is listed as a deliverable in the 2026-09-21 handover. It is not present in the sources.
